# Imputation, QCing, and CBCL thresholding

This script is used to:

1. Assign train and test sets of the data
2. Remove neuroimaging data for participants who do not meet ABCD's QC
3. Impute missing data
4. Threshold CBCL behaviour measures (raw scores into normal (0), borderline (1), and clinical (2))

## Neuroimaging quality control

First identify which subjects have valid neuroimaging data.

```{r eval = FALSE}
mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t1 <- abcd_load(core_path("imaging/mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t1.csv"))
mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t2 <- abcd_load(core_path("imaging/mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t2.csv"))
mri_y_qc_raw_rsfmr <- abcd_load(core_path("imaging/mri_y_qc_raw_rsfmr.csv"))
mri_y_qc_raw_dmr <- abcd_load(core_path("imaging/mri_y_qc_raw_dmr.csv"))

# Obtaining the QC'd subjects with complete neuroimaging data

## Baseline mTBI
rm_gord_cor_qc_mtbi <- abcdutils::qc_rsfmri(
    rm_gord_cor_mtbi,
    mri_y_qc_raw_rsfmr,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

rm_subc_cor_qc_mtbi <- abcdutils::qc_rsfmri(
    rm_subc_cor_mtbi,
    mri_y_qc_raw_rsfmr,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

dm_all_wmnd_qc_mtbi <- abcdutils::qc_dmri(
    dm_all_wmnd_mtbi,
    mri_y_qc_raw_dmr,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

sm_cort_sa_qc_mtbi <- abcdutils::qc_smri(
    sm_cort_sa_mtbi,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t1,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t2,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

sm_cort_t_qc_mtbi <- abcdutils::qc_smri(
    sm_cort_t_mtbi,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t1,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t2,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

sm_subc_v_qc_mtbi <- abcdutils::qc_smri(
    sm_subc_v_mtbi,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t1,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t2,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

## Uninjured
rm_gord_cor_qc_uninj <- abcdutils::qc_rsfmri(
    rm_gord_cor_uninj,
    mri_y_qc_raw_rsfmr,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

rm_subc_cor_qc_uninj <- abcdutils::qc_rsfmri(
    rm_subc_cor_uninj,
    mri_y_qc_raw_rsfmr,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

dm_all_wmnd_qc_uninj <- abcdutils::qc_dmri(
    dm_all_wmnd_uninj,
    mri_y_qc_raw_dmr,
    t = 0,
    no_na = FALSE
)

sm_cort_sa_qc_uninj <- abcdutils::qc_smri(
    sm_cort_sa_uninj,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t1,
    mri_y_qc_raw_smr_t2,

sm_cort_t_qc_uninj <- abcdutils::qc_smri(

write_csv(rm_gord_cor_qc_mtbi, input_path("rm_gord_cor_qc_mtbi.csv", TRUE))
write_csv(rm_subc_cor_qc_mtbi, input_path("rm_subc_cor_qc_mtbi.csv", TRUE))
```

## Train/Test split

To avoid having training and testing data inform each other during imputation, we assign the splits prior to the imputation.

```{r}
mtbi_split <- train_test_assign(
    train_frac = 0.8,
    subjects = mtbi_subjects$"subjectkey"
)

mtbi_train <- mtbi_subjects[mtbi_split$"split" == "train", ]
mtbi_test <- mtbi_subjects[mtbi_split$"split" == "test", ]

write_csv(mtbi_train, sub_path("mtbi_subjects_train.csv", TRUE))
write_csv(mtbi_test, sub_path("mtbi_subjects_test.csv", TRUE))

mtbi_train <- read_csv(sub_path("2024_01_26_mtbi_subjects_train.csv"))
mtbi_test <- read_csv(sub_path("2024_01_26_mtbi_subjects_test.csv"))
```

# Imputation

Data will be imputed under the following schemes:
- 5 imputations of mTBI data alone
- 5 imputations of uninjured data alone
- 5 imputations of mTBI + uninjured data together

Resulting in 10 versions of the mTBI data and 10 versions of the uninjured data.

# Imputing missing data

SNF requires complete data as input for integration.

We face a few oddities that may impact the validity of using a multiple imputation approach:

Neuroimaging data, which accounts for the majority of the individual features, are either completely removed or completely present for most subjects.
We proceed by not including those subjects who are missing neuroimaging data or who have neuroimaging data that did not pass checks for quality control.

Though this work is an exploratory clustering analysis that is designed to reveal insights about patterns across all variables, the experimental design used focuses on those insights particular relevant to better understanding behavioural impairments following concussion.
Our post-concussion assessments of behavioural impairment come from the CBCL and SDS.
CBCL data, which comprises a wide set of features, is either completely missing or completely present.

## Checking for excessive collinearity

```{r}
# Restrict to only shared variables

keep_numeric <- function(df) {
    df <- numcol_to_numeric(df)
    classes <- as.vector(sapply(df, class))
    df <- df[, classes == "numeric", drop = FALSE]
    return(df)
}

correlation_heatmap <- function(data_list, order = NULL) {
    dl_df <- collapse_dl(data_list)
    numeric_dl_df <- keep_numeric(dl_df)
    correlation_matrix <- cor(numeric_dl_df)
    if (is.null(order)) {
        heatmap <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(correlation_matrix)
    } else {
        heatmap <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(
            correlation_matrix[order, order],
            cluster_rows = FALSE,
            cluster_columns = FALSE
        )
    }
    drawn_heatmap <- ComplexHeatmap::draw(heatmap)
    order <- ComplexHeatmap::row_order(drawn_heatmap)
    results <- list(
        "correlation_matrix" = correlation_matrix,
        "heatmap" = heatmap,
        "order" = order
    )
    return(results)
}

# First pass to extract the order of columns
```

## Imputing missing data

Generating three different sets of 5:

- Imputing mTBI alone (5 datasets)
- Imputing uninjured alone (5 datasets)
- Imputing mTBI and uninjured together (5 datasets)

```{r eval = FALSE}
    dplyr::select(-"subjectkey") |>
    data.frame()

    dplyr::select(-"subjectkey") |>

# Functions to check the biggest correlations
big_correlations <- function(df, threshold = 0) {
    df <- na.omit(df)
    correlations <- cor(df)
    diag(correlations) <- 0
    abs_cor <- abs(correlations)
    pairs <- t(combn(colnames(abs_cor), 2))
    paired_cors <- data.frame(pairs, cor = abs_cor[pairs])
    paired_cors <- paired_cors[paired_cors$"cor" > threshold, ]
    return(paired_cors)
}

predictor_candidates <- function(df, threshold = 0) {
    df <- big_correlations(df, threshold)
    variables <- c(df$"X1", df$"X2") |> unique()
    max_cor_df <- data.frame(
        variable = as.character(),
        max_cor = as.numeric()
    )
    i <- 0
    while (nrow(df) > 0) {
        i <- i + 1
        print(i)
        row_with_max_cor <- which(df$"cor" == max(df$"cor"))[1]
        var_with_max_cor <- df[row_with_max_cor, "X1"]
        max_cor <- df[row_with_max_cor, "cor"]
        max_cor_df <- rbind(
            max_cor_df,
            data.frame(
                variable = var_with_max_cor,
                max_cor = max_cor
            )
        )
        df <- df |>
            dplyr::filter(X1 != var_with_max_cor & X2 != var_with_max_cor)
    }
    return(max_cor_df)
}
```

```{r}
pull_imputed_vars <- function(original_df, imputed_df, partition = NULL) {
    if (!is.null(partition)) {
        original_rows <- nrow(original_df)
        start <- original_rows * partition + 1
        end <- original_rows * (partition + 1)
        partitioned_df <- imputed_df[start:end, colnames(original_df)]
        return(partitioned_df)
    } else {
        df <- imputed_df[, colnames(original_df)]
        return(df)
    }
}
```

```{r}
check_rows <- function(lst, rows) {
    status <- lst |>
        lapply(
            function(x) {
                nrow(x) == rows
            }
        ) |> unlist() |> all()
    return(status)
}
```

## Convert the raw CBCL scores into thresholded ones

Scores are transformed according to percentiles amongst the entire baseline ABCD sample:

* Normal: < 95%
* Borderline: 95% - 98%
* Clinical: > 98%

Percentiles are calculated within sex groups.
Typical CBCL norming separates boys and girls as well as the 6-11 and 12-18 age groups, however this sample is only 9-10 years old.

```{r}
gish_p_gi <- abcd_load(core_path("gender-identity-sexual-health/gish_p_gi.csv"))
sex <- get_sex(gish_p_gi, t = 0)
sex <- dplyr::filter(sex, sex %in% c("M", "F"))

baseline_cbcl <- mh_p_cbcl |>
    dplyr::filter(eventname == "baseline_year_1_arm_1") |>
    dplyr::select(subjectkey, dplyr::starts_with("cbcl_scr_syn_")) |>
    dplyr::select(subjectkey, dplyr::ends_with("_r")) |>
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::contains(c("internal", "external", "totprob"))) |>
    na.omit()
baseline_cbcl <- dplyr::inner_join(baseline_cbcl, sex)

# 11857 rows
nrow(baseline_cbcl)

baseline_cbcl_m <- baseline_cbcl |>
    dplyr::filter(sex == "M") |>
    dplyr::select(-sex, -subjectkey)
baseline_cbcl_f <- baseline_cbcl |>
    dplyr::filter(sex == "F") |>
    dplyr::select(-sex, -subjectkey)

baseline_cbcl <- baseline_cbcl |>
    dplyr::select(-subjectkey, -sex)

# Matrix storing the normal-borderline-clinical thresholds
thresholds <- matrix(nrow = 2, ncol = ncol(baseline_cbcl))
colnames(thresholds) <- colnames(baseline_cbcl)
rownames(thresholds) <- c("95", "98")

for (i in seq_len(ncol(baseline_cbcl))) {
    quantiles <- quantile(baseline_cbcl[, i], probs = c(0.95, 0.98))
    thresholds[1, i] <- quantiles["95%"]
    thresholds[2, i] <- quantiles["98%"]
}

# Matrix storing the normal-borderline-clinical thresholds

colnames(thresholds_m) <- colnames(baseline_cbcl_m)
rownames(thresholds_m) <- c("95", "98")

for (i in seq_len(ncol(baseline_cbcl_f))) {

}

apply_cbcl_thresholds <- function(cbcl_df, threshold_matrix) {
    for (i in colnames(cbcl_df)) {
        if (i %in% colnames(threshold_matrix)) {
            borderline <- threshold_matrix["95", i]
            clinical <- threshold_matrix["98", i]
            col <- cbcl_df[, i]
            cbcl_df <- cbcl_df |> dplyr::mutate(
                "{i}" := dplyr::case_when(
                    col < borderline ~ 0,
                    col >= borderline & col <= clinical ~ 1,
                    col > clinical ~ 2,
                    TRUE ~ NA
                )
            )
        }
    }
    return(cbcl_df)
}

sex_norm <- function(cbcl_df, sex_df, m_thresh, f_thresh) {
    full_df <- dplyr::inner_join(cbcl_df, sex_df, by = "subjectkey")
    m_df <- full_df |>
        dplyr::filter(sex == 0) |>
        dplyr::select(-sex)
    f_df <- full_df |>
        dplyr::filter(sex == 1) |>
        dplyr::select(-sex)
    for (i in colnames(m_df)) {
        if (i %in% colnames(m_thresh)) {
            borderline <- m_thresh["95", i]
            clinical <- m_thresh["98", i]
            col <- m_df[, i]
            m_df <- m_df |> dplyr::mutate(
                "{i}" := dplyr::case_when(
                    col < borderline ~ 0,
                    col >= borderline & col <= clinical ~ 1,
                    col > clinical ~ 2,
                    TRUE ~ NA
                )
            )
        }
    }
    for (i in colnames(f_df)) {
        if (i %in% colnames(f_thresh)) {
            borderline <- f_thresh["95", i]
            clinical <- f_thresh["98", i]
            col <- f_df[, i]
            f_df <- f_df |> dplyr::mutate(
                "{i}" := dplyr::case_when(
                    col < borderline ~ 0,
                    col >= borderline & col <= clinical ~ 1,
                    col > clinical ~ 2,
                    TRUE ~ NA
                )
            )
        }
    }
    normed_df <- rbind(m_df, f_df)
    return(normed_df)
}
```

## Constructing data_lists

We have:

* 1 original unimputed mTBI dataset
* 1 original unimputed uninjured dataset
* 5 imputed mTBI datasets
* 5 imputed uninjured datasets
* 5 imputed mTBI + uninjured datasets

For the sake of brevity, these will be referred to with the following notation:

* m = mTBI
* u = uninjured
* p = pooled
* 0 = original (unimputed)
* 1-5 = imputed dataset number

Here I am!

```{r}
###############################################################################
# mTBI-alone data lists
###############################################################################
data_list_m1 <- generate_data_list(
    list(as_mem_daze_mtbi_train_imp_1, "as_mem_daze", "AS", "discrete"),
    list(as_mechanism_mtbi_train_imp_1, "as_mechanism", "AS", "categorical"),
    list(as_loc_mtbi_train_imp_1, "as_loc", "AS", "discrete"),
    list(d_interview_age_mtbi_train_imp_1, "d_age", "D", "discrete"),
    list(d_mtbi_age_mtbi_train_imp_1, "d_mtbi_age", "D", "discrete"),
    list(d_sex_mtbi_train_imp_1, "d_sex", "D", "discrete"),
    list(d_income_mtbi_train_imp_1, "d_income", "D", "ordinal"),
    list(d_race_mtbi_train_imp_1, "d_race", "D", "discrete"),
    list(d_pubertal_status_mtbi_train_imp_1, "d_pubertal", "D", "discrete"),
    list(mh_headaches_mtbi_train_imp_1, "mh_headaches", "MH", "discrete"),
    list(mh_mtbi_count_mtbi_train_imp_1, "mh_mtbi_count", "MH", "discrete"),
    list(sm_subc_v_mtbi_train_imp_1, "sm_subc_v", "N", "continuous"),
    list(sm_cort_t_mtbi_train_imp_1, "sm_cort_t", "N", "continuous"),
    list(sm_cort_sa_mtbi_train_imp_1, "sm_cort_sa", "N", "continuous"),

    list(p_loneliness_mtbi_train_imp_1, "p_loneliness", "P", "discrete"),
```

## Renaming the initial data

```{r}
rename_data_list <- function(data_list, name_mapping) {
    data_list <- data_list |> lapply(
        function(x) {
            old_colnames <- colnames(x$"data")
            new_colnames <- old_colnames |> lapply(
                function(old_name) {
                    if (old_name %in% name_mapping) {
                        name_match <- which(name_mapping == old_name)
                        new_name <- names(name_mapping)[name_match]
                    } else {
                        new_name <- old_name
                    }
                    return(new_name)
                }
            )
            colnames(x$"data") <- new_colnames
            return(x)
        }
    )
    return(data_list)
}
```
